claim: Pakistan shot down six Indian fighter jets, including Rafale jets, during Operation Sindoor
details: Dassault Aviation CEO Eric Trappier stated that no Rafale was lost in combat; he attributed one Rafale loss to a technical failure at high altitude during a training mission, unrelated to any engagement with Pakistan.

Defence Secretary RK Singh called the use of 'Rafales' in the plural 'absolutely not correct', and CDS General Anil Chauhan called Pakistan's six-jet claim 'absolutely incorrect', while acknowledging some Indian aircraft losses in combat. India has said all pilots returned home.
An Indian Air Force tender document seeks a five-month 'bridge support' package covering all 36 Rafale aircraft, the same number India procured from France, consistent with an intact fleet.

A viral video purporting to show the Army Chief admitting six jets were lost was debunked by Newschecker as a deepfake: the real PTI footage from his January 13, 2026 press conference contains no mention of jet losses, and multiple AI detection tools flagged the clip.

sources.name: Zee News: Pakistan lying about shooting down Rafales, says Dassault CEO
Indian Defence News: India's Rafales were never downed during Operation Sindoor

summary: Pakistan's claim has no credible evidence. Dassault Aviation's CEO, India's Defence Secretary and the Chief of Defence Staff have all rejected it, and a recent IAF tender seeks support for the full fleet of 36 Rafales.

claim: Forwarded links and agent-run websites can complete Ladki Bahin e-KYC
details: Maharashtra's Women and Child Development department warned beneficiaries after a fake portal mimicking the official e-KYC site surfaced; several women reported being misled by agents directing them to unofficial websites.
No government officer calls, SMSes or WhatsApps asking for an Aadhaar OTP; applying and e-KYC are free and no paid agent service exists.
Victims should report at cybercrime.gov.in or call 1930; the scheme helpline is 181.
summary: Only the official portal ladakibahin.maharashtra.gov.in/ekyc is genuine; fraud sites mimicking it steal Aadhaar and bank details.

claim: Ladki Bahin monthly aid has been raised to Rs 2,100, with a Diwali bonus announced
details: The scheme continues to pay Rs 1,500 per month to eligible women; the state budget allocated Rs 26,500 crore for the current year and announced no hike.
A viral message claiming a government resolution had raised the amount to Rs 2,100 was declared false by the government.
There is no confirmed news of any Ladki Bahin Diwali bonus; new registrations are closed, and any site claiming registration has reopened is fake.
summary: The Rs 2,100 hike was an election promise that has not been implemented; a message claiming a government resolution raised the amount was declared false, and no Diwali bonus exists.

claim: India has stopped buying Russian oil
details: In February 2026 Trump claimed India would stop buying Russian oil; the Indian government made no such statement, and the MEA has said sourcing is based on energy security and evolving market dynamics.
India is the world's largest importer of Russian seaborne crude, averaging 1.8 million barrels per day in 2026, ahead of China at 1.2 million, as per ship-tracking data.
After Trump waived the Graham Act sanctions and tariff threats on October 16, 2026, analysts expect Indian refiners to continue buying Russian crude near current levels.
summary: The claim came from US President Donald Trump, not New Delhi. India never made such a commitment and imported about 1.82 million barrels per day of Russian crude in September 2026.

claim: A decoction of wheat barley gum and black seeds can cure diabetes
details: Vishvas News investigated the viral message, which invoked the names of two doctors to appear credible, and rated the cure claim misleading.
There is no permanent cure for diabetes; some Type-2 patients can achieve remission through monitored weight loss, but remission is an ongoing state, not a guaranteed cure, and Type-1 has no cure.
Experts advise consulting a doctor before changing or stopping medication based on viral health forwards.
summary: No scientific evidence supports the claim. Diabetes has no permanent cure, and patients should not alter medication based on viral health forwards.

claim: The SIR of electoral rolls is a deliberate scheme to delete opposition voters (the 'vote chori' allegation)
details: Rahul Gandhi and INDIA bloc leaders alleged 'vote chori' through the SIR; Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar rejected the allegation and challenged Rahul Gandhi to file an affidavit or apologise.

ECI data for Bihar: the draft roll of August 1, 2025 showed about 65 lakh names absent against a June 24 roll of 7.89 crore; the ECI breakdown was about 22 lakh deceased, 36 lakh permanently migrated or untraceable, and 7 lakh enrolled elsewhere. After the claims and objections period, the final roll of September 30, 2025 stood at about 7.42 crore, and the ECI reported zero appeals against the final roll.

Transparency gaps are documented: the Supreme Court ordered deletion lists published in searchable form in August 2025; the ECI issued an October 15, 2026 order for readable rolls and change lists only after sustained opposition pressure; the Reporters' Collective found the EC's software had no category to tag any voter as a foreign national; and the Indian Express reported that two Election Commissioners recorded at least 14 written objections to SIR decisions taken without their approval.

sources.name: The Siasat Daily (citing The Reporters' Collective)

summary: Opposition leaders allege systematic deletion of voters through the Special Intensive Revision; the Election Commission rejects this and attributes removals to dead, shifted and duplicate entries. Independent evidence of systematic targeting is inconclusive.

claim: Tesla has unveiled a flying car that anyone can buy and fly
details: At SpaceX's McGregor, Texas test site, a driverless Roadster prototype used 10 cold-gas thrusters fed by compressed air tanks to roll upright mid-air, hover briefly, jump over Tesla vehicles and land on its wheels.
It was a controlled demonstration of a prototype, not a consumer flying car; production is planned only for 2028, and Tesla says 0-60 mph takes under one second.
Tesla's reservation page explicitly notes the cold-gas thruster package 'is not approved for public road use', and Elon Musk said on stage that legality would depend on the jurisdiction.
summary: The new Roadster did briefly fly in a controlled driverless stunt on October 15, 2026, but calling it a consumer flying car overstates what Tesla showed; Tesla's own fine print says the thruster package is not approved for public road use.

claim: Viral social media posts claim IIT Baba Abhay Singh died; similar posts claim other celebrities have died
details: Hisar Police clarified that the body recovered from a bedroom in Hisar's PLA area was that of Rahul Jain, not Abhay Singh; the viral posts misrepresented the incident.
A Jackie Chan death rumour used a black-and-white photo marked 1954-2026 and crossed 8 million views; a community note flagged it false, and Chan appeared publicly in Singapore in July 2026.
Police urged the public to verify death claims through reliable sources before sharing them online.
summary: IIT Baba Abhay Singh is alive; Hisar Police confirmed the body in the viral claim was Rahul Jain. Similar recent death hoaxes, including one about Jackie Chan, were also debunked.

claim: A video shows Indians spitting on the Bangladesh flag in retaliation for the Tagore mural vandalism in Dhaka
details: The Quint's WebQoof traced the footage to a Facebook post of December 11, 2024; a 'Pearl' shop sign in the clip matched Pearl Salon in Ghatkopar East, Mumbai, via Google Maps imagery.
The video had previously resurfaced in December 2025 with a different misleading claim linking it to another Bangladesh-related incident.
The Tagore mural defacement outside Dhaka's Shilpakala Academy happened on October 10, 2026, long after the video was filmed, so it cannot show retaliation for it.
summary: The footage is from Ghatkopar East, Mumbai, dating to at least December 2024, and has no connection to the October 10, 2026 Dhaka incident.

claim: Air India flight AI2030 was hijacked on October 14, 2026
details: Flight AI2030 (Frankfurt to Delhi, Boeing 787-9) was diverted to Jaipur on October 14, 2026, after ATC reported receiving squawk code 7500, the code for unlawful interference.

The pilot-in-command denied transmitting the emergency code; later reports citing aviation officials suspect a malfunction in an ATC radar system in Mumbai. The exact cause is unestablished and the DGCA investigation is ongoing.
Security agencies cleared the aircraft and crew in Jaipur; all passengers were safe and the flight completed its journey to Delhi the same day.
summary: The hijack alert was a false alarm. The pilot denied squawking code 7500, investigators suspect a Mumbai ATC radar glitch, and the DGCA is investigating.

claim: Dozens of people were killed in the Vaishali boat tragedy of October 13, 2026
details: A private boat carrying villagers to a feast capsized in the Ganga near Rampur Shyamchand village, Raghopur, Vaishali district, on the night of October 13, 2026.
District Magistrate Varsha Singh confirmed 13 deaths, all children below 15 years of age, and 6 rescued; search and rescue operations ended on October 14 with the toll unchanged.
RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav claimed 14 bodies were recovered, but no official count has exceeded 13.
summary: The district administration confirmed 13 deaths and 6 rescued; viral claims of much higher tolls are unsubstantiated and search operations ended with the toll unchanged.

claim: Zoho has frozen annual salary hikes for employees this year
details: In a public post on X on October 13, Vembu said: 'We have told our employees that we cannot have our usual pay increase this year', and said he had apologised to staff.
Reasons cited: a massive fourfold increase in data-centre server prices, rapidly rising AI usage expenses, an uncertain software market and a challenging geopolitical backdrop.
Zoho has also cut its marketing budget and kept headcount flat for 18 months; Vembu said the company will work hard to avoid mass layoffs but called the software jobs outlook grim.
summary: The claim is true. Founder Sridhar Vembu announced on October 13, 2026 that Zoho will skip its usual annual pay hikes, citing a fourfold rise in server prices and soaring AI costs.

claim: A real Gen-Z woman's video demolishes the CJP protest with facts
details: The Quint's WebQoof traced the nearly three-minute video to the Instagram account 'Sifat Sangh', which posted it on October 7, 2026; the woman's appearance differs from the account's real photos.

Hive Moderation's tool scored the video element at 99.9 percent and the audio track at 99.4 percent likelihood of being AI-generated; Hiya's deepfake voice detector scored the audio 3 out of 100 for authenticity.
Google's SynthID detector also flagged AI watermarks in the clip.
summary: The video is AI-generated, not a real person speaking. Multiple AI detectors scored it near-certain synthetic, and the account behind it shows a different-looking woman in its other posts.

claim: Viral videos show the October 10, 2026 Delhi CJP protest at Jantar Mantar
details: Factly found the clips were old or unrelated: one showing a huge crowd is from a Sealdah, West Bengal protest of July 25, 2026; another showing security personnel thrashing a youth has been online since at least July 23, 2026.

Boom Live debunked a February 21, 2024 PTI video of the farmers' protest shared as gunshots and fatalities on October 10; Delhi Police called it fake and no credible report records any fatalities at the protest.
The Quint found a March 29, 2026 bikers video from West Bengal falsely shared as Hindu groups reaching Jantar Mantar to counter the protest.
summary: Fact-checkers traced the clips to July-August 2026 protests, a March 2026 bikers rally and a February 2024 farmers protest video; none shows the October 10 Jantar Mantar protest.

claim: A viral video shows a landslide and flash flood in Nepal's Rasuwa district killing 270 people
details: Geolocation via Google Earth matched buildings and terrain in the clip to Dharali, Uttarakhand, India, not Nepal's Rasuwa district.
The August 2025 Dharali disaster caused 5 fatalities and over 50 missing persons, not the claimed 270 dead and 1,450 missing.
The original 2025 event was widely reported by Indian media including DNA India.
summary: The footage is from Dharali village, Uttarkashi, Uttarakhand, India, on August 6, 2025, and the death figures in the claim do not match the actual 2025 toll.

claim: The radio signal detected from Beta Pictoris b is evidence of alien technology.
details: The bursts (0.85 to 3.5 GHz) were rapid, recurring, and highly circularly polarized, matching auroral emission, not an artificial signal. The paper attributes them to magnetosphere-ionosphere coupling at the planet.

The finding matters because it gave the first direct measurement of an exoplanet's magnetic field strength: at least 1.25 kilogauss, more than 200 times Jupiter's field, which allows study of how planetary magnetic fields form.

The signal was confirmed to come from the planet, not its star, by lining up radio images against distant quasars as fixed markers. The host star is magnetically quiet, which made the detection possible.
The study is a preprint and had not yet completed peer review at the time of our reporting, so experts urged caution even though the natural explanation is the only one the data supports.

sources.name: arXiv: Discovery of radio emission from the exoplanet beta Pictoris b
NDTV Profit: First Radio Signal From A Planet Beyond Our Solar System Detected - No, It's Not Aliens

summary: The signal is natural auroral radio emission, not a technosignature. A team led by Kevin Ortiz Ceballos at the Center for Astrophysics (Harvard and Smithsonian) used South Africa's MeerKAT array to record repeating radio bursts from the gas giant Beta Pictoris b, about 63 light-years away. The paper, posted on arXiv on September 15, 2026 and awaiting peer review, identifies the emission as auroral, produced by the same electron cyclotron maser process seen at Jupiter and Earth.

claim: EAM S. Jaishankar predicted a major global food crisis specifically in 2027.
details: The exact quote, reported by PTI, The Hindu, and The Tribune: "So there is gonna be a major food crisis probably, you know, in the coming months." No year was specified.
The remarks were made at an Asia Society event in New York on Monday, September 28, 2026, on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly high-level week, not at a 2027 forecast session.

The crisis drivers he cited were the Ukraine and Iran-Gulf conflicts disrupting grain shipments (especially through the Black Sea) and fertiliser production, which he said would strain Global South economies.

Our own first reel on this story (October 4, 2026) carried the headline "a major global food crisis is coming in 2027." We corrected this in a follow-up carousel the same day with the exact quote, and note the correction here.

sources.name: The Hindu: EAM Jaishankar warns of 'major food crisis' in coming months
The Tribune (ANI): Jaishankar after meeting UN chief Guterres

summary: Jaishankar warned of a major food crisis but gave no year. Speaking at the Asia Society in New York on September 28, 2026, he said there would be a major food crisis "probably in the coming months," citing the Ukraine and Iran-Gulf conflicts, Black Sea grain disruption, and fertiliser shortages. The 2027 date came from the wording of our own earlier reel headline, which we corrected in a follow-up carousel carrying his exact quote.

claim: The US and Australia shut their diplomatic missions in Brazil because of a confirmed security threat before the October 2026 election.
details: The US State Department cited security concerns but gave no further detail on the nature of the threat or any link to the October 4 election. It did not say when services would resume.
Australia's ambassador, Sophie Davies, said the closure cited the US alert and advised Australians to avoid US diplomatic facilities. She did not cite an independent Australian assessment.

Brazil's federal police said the search-and-seizure warrants followed cooperation with foreign intelligence agencies, but no evidence backed the reported threat, and no suspects linked to criminal organisations were identified.

The closures came two days before the presidential first round (Lula vs Flavio Bolsonaro). The Workers' Party called them "unprecedented" and suggested political motives; the US did not link the closures to the election.

sources.name: Al Jazeera: US and Australia suspend diplomatic operations in Brazil before election
New Indian Express (AP): US and Australia suspend consular services in Brazil

summary: The closures did happen, but the threat was never confirmed. On October 2, 2026, the US suspended consular services at its embassy and consulates in Brazil citing unspecified security concerns, and Australia closed its Brasilia embassy citing the US alert. Brazil's federal police carried out preventive raids in Sao Paulo and the Federal District but said investigators found no evidence corroborating the initially reported threat and identified no suspects linked to criminal organisations.

claim: Skeletons found at Mohenjo-daro prove that invading Aryans massacred the city's inhabitants and ended the Indus civilization.
details: Wheeler's case rested on skeleton groups at Mohenjo-daro, read as victims of invaders. For a single massacre they would need to come from the same, latest level; they do not, so they cannot be tied to one event, let alone an invasion.
No invader's weapons or material culture have been found at Harappan sites, while excavation shows cultural continuity, a gradual devolution of the urban tradition, not a sudden violent end.

The Rakhigarhi genome (one individual, published in Cell, September 2019 by Shinde and colleagues with Harvard Medical School and the Birbal Sahni Institute) indicates the Harappans were an indigenous South Asian population with ancestry traceable before 7000 BCE.

The study's authors argued this rejects Steppe pastoral or ancient Iranian farmers as the source of Harappan ancestry and treats the skeletons as flood victims and normal burials, not war dead. Migration remains an active academic debate, but the massacre reading of the Mohenjo-daro skeletons is not supported.

sources.name: Times of India: DNA analysis of Rakhigarhi remains challenges Aryan invasion theory
The Week: New DNA study debunks Aryan invasion theory

summary: The skeletal evidence does not show a single massacre. Sir Mortimer Wheeler interpreted scattered skeletons at Mohenjo-daro as victims of an Aryan invasion, but the remains come from different stratigraphic levels, some from deposits that accumulated after the site was abandoned, which is inconsistent with one violent event. Archaeologist George F. Dales, who excavated at Mohenjo-daro, called the massacre account "mythical," and genome sequencing of a 4,500-year-old Rakhigarhi skeleton (Shinde et al., Cell, September 2019) found no Steppe ancestry in the Harappan population.

claim: A video shows a Punjab Police officer saying the LPU accused is a BJP worker and Amit Shah's nephew
details: The original footage shows Phagwara SP Major Singh discussing the LPU allegations and stating that police had not received any complaint; he never names a BJP worker or Amit Shah's nephew.
AI detection tools indicated the audio was likely manipulated, and PIB Fact Check also confirmed the video was digitally altered using AI technology.
Police said they found no evidence so far to substantiate the underlying LPU rape allegation, which triggered protests and vandalism on September 27, 2026.
summary: The video is AI-manipulated. The real footage shows the officer saying no complaint was received; the accusatory audio was fabricated.

claim: The 'VRK Diet' can permanently cure Type-1 diabetes, so patients can stop insulin
details: Raidurgam Police registered an FIR against Telugu health influencer Veeramachaneni Ramakrishna and Dr Koteshwara Rao after a complaint by a Type-1 diabetic.

The 30-year-old complainant, diabetic since 2018, was allegedly advised to stop insulin at the VRK Health Care Centre in Hyderabad in September 2025; two days later he was hospitalised with diabetic ketoacidosis and severe dehydration.
Doctors warn that stopping insulin for Type-1 diabetes can be fatal; there is no permanent cure, only management.
summary: The claim is false and dangerous. An FIR was filed after a patient who stopped insulin on this advice suffered diabetic ketoacidosis; Type-1 diabetes has no cure.

claim: A viral video shows the first visuals of the August 2026 Nepal floods
details: Reverse image search traced the video to a Mexican user's Facebook post of July 27, 2026, carrying Peru hashtags.
Spanish media reported the same visuals as an avalanche captured by tourists at Lake Humantay, Cusco, Peru, crediting the original uploader.
The surroundings in the footage match Google Maps imagery of the lake and not the Nepal-Tibet border region.
summary: The clip shows an avalanche at Lake Humantay in Cusco, Peru, uploaded on July 27, 2026, weeks before the Nepal floods of August 26, 2026.

claim: A video shows a Chinese-built dam collapsing and causing the August 2026 Nepal floods
details: AFP's fact check found the dam-collapse video contains visual errors indicating it was generated using AI.
The actual trigger was a high-altitude glacial collapse that sent ice and rock debris downstream, according to the US Geological Survey.
The August 26 disaster killed at least 1,385 people and left over 5,500 missing; Nepal's foreign minister warned of the growing climate threat in the Himalayas.
summary: The dam-collapse video is AI-generated. The real Nepal floods were triggered by a glacial collapse, not a dam failure.

claim: A video shows people being washed away in Nepal's August 2026 floods
details: The Quint's WebQoof found visual inconsistencies: skyscrapers appear in the background, while the flooded regions of Nepal are hilly and mountainous.
The same video existed on Instagram on July 11, predating the August 26 floods by over a month.
Reverse image searches found no credible news source sharing the clip as genuine Nepal flood footage.
summary: The video is AI-generated, not real footage. An identical clip was posted on Instagram on July 11, 2026, more than a month before the floods.

claim: A video shows Union Minister Piyush Goyal threatening student protesters in Delhi
details: PIB's Fact Check unit debunked the clip as a deepfake on September 3, 2026; it falsely portrays threats against student protesters.
PIB urged citizens to report suspicious content via WhatsApp at +91 8799711259 or email factcheck@pib.gov.in, and to avoid forwarding until an official handle confirms.
Creating or knowingly amplifying such fakes can invite prosecution under the IT Act's impersonation provisions and BNS Section 356 for criminal defamation.
summary: PIB Fact Check confirmed the video is a deepfake; the threats against student protesters were fabricated.

claim: A video shows the Army Chief admitting the IAF lost six jets in Operation Sindoor
details: Newschecker traced the clip to PTI's footage of the Army Chief's annual press conference of January 13, 2026; the authentic video contains no mention of IAF losses or six jets.
Deepware Scanner, Resemble AI, Aurigin.ai and Hiya's deepfake voice detector all flagged the clip's audio and video as AI-manipulated.
The Army's official social media handles carry no such admission; the viral clip layered a fabricated voiceover onto the genuine footage.
summary: The clip is a deepfake. The real footage is the Army Chief's January 2026 press conference, which contains no admission of jet losses; the voiceover was AI-fabricated.

claim: The government announced a Rs 4,000 Raksha Bandhan bonus under PM-KISAN
details: PIB confirmed that no festive payment bonus has been announced under PM-KISAN; the scheme pays Rs 6,000 per year in three equal instalments of Rs 2,000.
Fraudulent creators used AI tools to mimic official news announcers, official logos and fake dates to deceive viewers.
No government notification or official handle supports the claim.
summary: No such bonus exists. PIB debunked AI-generated videos that mimicked news anchors to spread the false claim.

claim: A video shows Dharmendra Pradhan threatening to expose the BJP after resigning as Education Minister
details: Factly found the video is fabricated, using an AI-generated voice clone layered over NDTV news footage; Pradhan made no such statements after his resignation.
The anchor segment was taken from a July 26, 2026 NDTV YouTube video that discusses the resignation but contains no such speech.
Pradhan's visuals came from a May 2026 press conference on the NEET paper leak; no media report or his own social media contains the alleged remarks.
summary: The clip is an AI deepfake. The voice is cloned and the visuals are stitched from unrelated NDTV footage; Pradhan never made the alleged remarks.

claim: RBI will withdraw all paper currency notes and replace them with plastic notes by June 30, 2026
details: PIB Fact Check stated: 'According to RBI, there are no plans to withdraw paper currency notes or replace them with plastic currency notes by June 30, 2026.'
The viral messages used edited videos and misleading captions to look official; PIB confirmed the material is digitally altered and tied to no RBI communication.
RBI has only discussed polymer notes at a preliminary stage; there is no exchange deadline and no nationwide replacement programme.
summary: False. PIB Fact Check debunked the claim on June 9, 2026: the RBI has made no such announcement and existing paper currency remains valid.

claim: PM-KISAN registration links and 'PM KISSAN.apk' files shared on WhatsApp are official
details: Kerala authorities warned that files named 'PM KISSAN.apk' can secretly install malicious apps that steal data, control the device and siphon money from linked bank accounts.
Fraudsters send fake SMS messages such as 'PM Kisan payment credited, click to confirm bank details' and run cloned websites that harvest Aadhaar and bank information.
Official channels only: the pmkisan.gov.in portal, Common Service Centres, or the official app from the Google Play Store; the official helpline is 155261 and the cyber helpline is 1930.
summary: The government never sends PM-KISAN registration links by SMS or WhatsApp; the circulating APK files install malware that can empty bank accounts.
